record.original_question: Given an arrangement (L, P) of construction lines and registration marks in the Euclidean plane, where every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P, which such arrangements also satisfy the additional linear-space condition that every pair of distinct points in P lies on some line of L? Equivalently, which arrangements of this kind form a finite linear space?

evidence.quote: Which arrangements of construction lines and registration marks satisfy this assumption? Put in another way, which arrangements form a (finite) linear space?
I have not been able to identify other arrangements containing shapes that define linear spaces (i.e., in which any two distinct points lie on a line).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let L be a finite collection of distinct lines in the Euclidean plane and let P be a finite set of points in the plane satisfying the following two incidence axioms:

(i) every point of P is the intersection of at least two lines belonging to L;
(ii) any two non-parallel lines in L meet in a (unique) point that lies in P.

Such a pair (L, P) will be called an arrangement.

Recall that a finite linear space is a pair (P, L) consisting of a finite point set P and a family L of subsets of P (called lines), each of size at least two, such that every pair of distinct points of P is contained in exactly one line of L.

Problem: Characterize all arrangements (L, P) in the above sense with the additional property that every pair of distinct points of P lies on some line of L. Equivalently, determine which arrangements (L, P) of construction lines and registration marks (in the sense of (i)–(ii)) yield a finite linear space when each line ℓ ∈ L is identified with its set of incident points ℓ ∩ P.
artifact.category_tag: finite linear spaces and line arrangements
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a list of open problems on arrangements determining shapes. No subsequent paper resolving the characterization of which such arrangements form finite linear spaces was located; the author explicitly states only a few examples have been identified.
